title: Why scientists stop making testable predictions

beats.narr: What if science paid you more for telling stories... than for testing ideas?
Picture two researchers. One makes a risky, testable guess. The other waits, sees the data, then tells a flexible story.
The guesser wins big when they're right, and pays a price when they're wrong. The storyteller? Always a small, sure reward.
Here's the catch. A guess has to be right more than two times in three to be worth making. At six in ten, the safe story pays better.
beats.axis_label: How often a guess is right

beats.narr: So testable research slowly dies out. In the model, the testers shrink until only one in ten is left.
But raise the reward for being right, and it flips. Now the safe story is the one that dies out.
